body: :+1: Glad I'm not the only one that was seeing this, thanks for creating the issue @taion, saved a lot of time :)

Well you're shadowing two bindings created from a single construct, so this makes sense. You could argue it's not necessary to warn about both shadowings, but then this would be an enhancement, not a bug.
I just filed this as requested per https://github.com/eslint/eslint/pull/2547#issuecomment-102644231. I do think it's fairly unintuitive and confusing to see this error twice, though.
@michaelficarra which two bindings are you referring to?

Oh wow, had no idea that was the case. Thanks for explaining.

Even so, this behavior is confusing, so we should fix it.
Is that also the root cause of #2545, then? Would be good to take out the special-casing logic there if this can be resolved, if so.

issue.title: Fix: Improve around function/class names of `no-shadow` (fixes #2556, #2552)

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
I changed the logic to check function names and class names.
Basically it checks shadowing around function/class names. But it handles variable initializers specially in order to be compatible with declarations such as `var a = function a() { };`.

And I added [only one line](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/compare/eslint:master...mysticatea:fix-function-name-and-class-name-of-shadow?expand=1#diff-bb960ca8871dafb0bbd3959858e00231R68) to fix #2552.
If I should separate PR for this, I will do.
